He played for the [[Detroit Pistons]], [[Sacramento Kings]] and [[Denver Nuggets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), as well as the [[Reno Bighorns]], [[Iowa Energy]] and [[Grand Rapids Drive]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA Development League]]. He was born in the [[Chicago metropolitan area]] and was raised there until the age of 13, at which point he moved to live with an uncle in North Carolina so that he could live a better life. He attended four different high schools, but eventually became one of the top ten high school basketball prospects in the class of 2011. He played for [[USA Basketball]] in the 2010 [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]]. Early in his senior year, he tore his [[anterior cruciate ligament]] (ACL), rendering him incapable of playing the remainder of the season. He played his [[true freshman]] season with the [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor Bears]] as a [[Forward (basketball)|forward]] for the [[2011–12 Baylor Bears basketball team|2011–12 team]]. In his freshman season, the team set school records for its best start (17–0), longest winning streak (17) and highest ranking (3/3). Following the [[2011–12 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season]], he was named the Big 12 co-Freshman of the Year and was recognized as an honorable mention All-Big 12 and a Big 12 All-Star Team selection by the Big 12 coaches. He was named Big 12 Freshman of the Year by ''[[Sporting News]]''. In the NBA, Miller had a modest role for most of his first two seasons. He began to get regular playing time midway through his second season, and in the final weeks of his second season he became an everyday starter due to injury. In [[2015–16 Euroleague|2016]], he earned an [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]] selection and was a member of the [[2015–16 ABA League]] champion, the [[2015–16 Basketball League of Serbia]] champion and the [[2016–17 Israeli Basketball State Cup]] winner. ==High school career== At age 13, his uncle Lamont Taylor from [[Fairmont, North Carolina]] took Miller in to get him away from the Chicago street life.{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111209163839/http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/articles/2010/11/01-NC-Deuce-Bello-Quincy-Miller-november-mag.aspx|archive-date=December 9, 2011|url=http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/articles/2010/11/01-NC-Deuce-Bello-Quincy-Miller-november-mag.aspx|title=Deuce Bello, Quincy Miller join forces, form feared hardwood duo|access-date=December 29, 2011|date=November 1, 2010|work=[[ESPN HS]]|author=Parker, Brandon}} He transferred from [[North Chicago High School]] and played his freshman season for Fairmont High School (North Carolina) before transferring to Quality Education Academy, where he grew {{convert|8|in|cm|1}} as a sophomore.{{cite web|url=http://www.usabasketball.com/bios/miller_quincy.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100706194836/http://www.usabasketball.com/bios/miller_quincy.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 6, 2010|title=Quincy Miller|access-date=December 29, 2011|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]}} Miller was relatively unknown until the 2009 Pangos All-American Camp and the Hoop Jamboree. Miller had begun playing AAU basketball for D-One Sports. Then by July 2009 he was a top 10 class of 2011 prospect by [[Scout.com]] and top 25 by ''[[PrepStar]]'' and had interest from [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]], [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/preps/basketball/2009-07-22-miller-gboa-challenge-of-champions_N.htm|title=Top recruit Miller gets a chance to play in front of top programs|access-date=December 30, 2011|date=July 22, 2009|work=[[USA Today]]|author=Sun, Victoria}} Late in Miller's 2009–10 junior season, he began receiving significant support from the 2010 ''[[ESPN HS]]'' [[Mr. Basketball USA]] voters who moved him into 11th place.{{cite web|url=http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/articles/2010/03/05-tracker-NHSI-opens-up-scenarios.aspx|title=Tracker: NHSI opens up scenarios|access-date=December 29, 2011|date=March 5, 2010|work=[[ESPN HS]]|author=Flores, Ronnie}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}{{cite web|url=http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/articles/2010/03/12-tracker-sullinger.aspx|title=Tracker: History in the making |access-date=December 29, 2011|date=March 13, 2010|work=[[ESPN HS]]|author=Flores, Ronnie}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} At the time, he was competing for Quality Education Academy in [[Winston-Salem, NC|Winston-Salem]].
